# V — Post-purchase: cancel and device return

**Specs:** `post-purchase-order-management` (all 4 scenarios: "Shipment state visible", "Partial shipment", "Return started", "Refund state visible"); D-040 adds **cancel before service start** (no spec scenario; tested through the task tests listed in Design)
**Depends on:** S, U · **Unblocks:** generated by verify-plan · **Decisions:** D-005, D-021, D-023, D-040, D-050, D-059
**Owner prerequisites:** none beyond OA-02 (storefront client has `manage_orders` and `manage_recurring_orders`; no `view_states`/`manage_states` is needed, see "State model") · **Skill refs:** `commercetools-storefront` (orders, returns), `commercetools-commerce-patterns` (recurring orders)

## Goal
On a signed-in customer's order page they can **cancel the whole order until its service-start date** (with a stored reason, the early-termination fee text shown, and monthly charges stopped), **request the return of a device within 30 days**, and **see shipments, parcels, tracking references and the separate goods/refund states** of returns. The cancel-order and device-return flows are not drawn: Junior design choice (D-068).

## Design

### 1. Planner defaults for the spec's open questions (single place)
- **Who owns the returns process of record:** the **commercetools Order holds the record** (`returnInfo` + our `returnRequest` field). Return processing (labels, receiving goods, restock, refund money, Order Edit settlement) is **out of scope** (D-040, D-059): staff or a future system moves the states through `setReturnShipmentState` / `setReturnPaymentState`; the storefront only **reads** them.
- **Returns window and scope:** **30 days for all devices** (no per-category rule), counted from the order's `createdAt` (v1 has no fulfilment system that stamps a delivery date, so a delivery date cannot be the trigger; a Planner default). Returnable lines: lines of kind **device** only (marker: the order line carries Q's acquisition fields, `line.acquisition != null`); equipment (routers) and services are not returnable online (constant `RETURNABLE_ONLY_ACQUISITION_LINES = true`). Q's lease "return at end of term" (Q §4 `RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 30`) is a different, later obligation and is **not** touched here.
- **A "delivered" order (spec wording) in v1:** nobody sets `shipmentState: Delivered` automatically, so a return request is allowed for any non-cancelled order inside the window (Planner default); the UI wording is "Return a device within 30 days of ordering".
- **Cancel window (D-023/D-040):** allowed while `now` is **strictly before 00:00 UTC of `custom.fields.serviceStartDate`** (the earliest service start on the order, written by U). Confirmed by the owner (D-062): phone and fixed-wireless plans have lead time 0 (D-023), so their order's start date is the order date and **a phone-only order is not cancellable online** (the cancel box then says so); a cable order has +5 days. Constant `CANCEL_WINDOW_INCLUSIVE = false` in `lib/config/postPurchase.ts`: setting it `true` allows the whole start day. Mixed bundles use the earliest start (U §5).
- **Equipment already shipped:** if `order.shipmentState ∈ {Shipped, Delivered, Partial}` the order is **not** cancellable online (reason `EQUIPMENT_SHIPPED`; Planner default, avoids half-cancelled shipments); an order with any existing return is also not cancellable (`HAS_RETURN`).
- **Guests (D-035):** guest orders have no account page, so no cancel/return online; the confirmation page sends them to `/support` (mailto). Cancel/return routes require `session.customerId` and `order.customerId === session.customerId`; any other case answers **404** `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` (never reveal existence).
- **Early-termination fee (ETF) display:** shown from the **label formula text stored on the order** (`labelSnapshot[lineId].etf`, e.g. cable `"$10 x months remaining"`, phone `"None"`, wireless `"$0"`; D-040) — **never computed**. In the cancel dialog each service line shows `{plan name}: {etf text}` and the sentence "You are cancelling before your service starts, so no early-termination fee is charged." (Planner default: before service start the fee does not apply; the formula is shown for transparency, as the label does.)
- **Payment effect of a cancel:** reversing/refunding the authorization or charge is **out of scope** (D-040); copy never promises a refund: "Your order is cancelled and no further charges will be made."

### 2. State model (no custom States)
Cancel uses the native `orderState` enum `Open | Confirmed | Complete | Cancelled` and the update action **`changeOrderState`** ([Orders API](https://docs.commercetools.com/api/projects/orders): `OrderChangeOrderStateAction {orderState}`, verified in the OpenAPI). Allowed transitions in v1: `Open → Cancelled`, `Confirmed → Cancelled`; `Complete` and `Cancelled` are final. **No `transitionState` / custom States** are created (there is no workflow beyond one transition; avoids the `view_states`/`manage_states` scopes that OA-02 does not list). The cancellation reason lives in the order custom field **`cancellation`** (String, JSON; field on type `malva-order`, G defines the type, U finalizes the order with it):
```ts
export interface CancellationRecord { reason: CancelReason; note?: string; cancelledAt: string /* ISO */; by: 'customer' }
export type CancelReason = 'changed_mind' | 'better_offer' | 'moving' | 'service_not_needed' | 'other';
```
Return state machine is the platform's, **read-only**: `ReturnShipmentState` entry `Advised` (request recorded) or `Returned`, then `BackInStock` or `Unusable`; `ReturnPaymentState` entry `NonRefundable` or `Initial`, then `Refunded` or `NotRefunded` ([docs](https://docs.commercetools.com/api/projects/orders#returnshipmentstate)). The storefront creates items in `Advised` (a **request**: goods not yet received) and never changes states afterwards.

### 3. Types (append to `lib/types.ts`, section `// ===== V: post-purchase =====`) and mapper
S owns `lib/mappers/order.ts` and the `Order` type; V **appends** these fields to `Order` (reuse S's names for anything S already maps: `orderNumber`, `createdAt`, `orderState`, `lines[]` with `id, name, quantity`) and maps them in the same mapper:
```ts
export interface OrderParcel { id: string; trackingId?: string; carrier?: string; items: { lineItemId: string; name: string; quantity: number }[] }
export interface OrderDelivery { id: string; createdAt: string; parcels: OrderParcel[]; items: { lineItemId: string; name: string; quantity: number }[] }
export type ReturnShipmentLabel = 'Advised' | 'Returned' | 'BackInStock' | 'Unusable';
export type ReturnPaymentLabel = 'NonRefundable' | 'Initial' | 'Refunded' | 'NotRefunded';
export interface OrderReturnItem { id: string; lineItemId: string; name: string; quantity: number; comment?: string; shipmentState: ReturnShipmentLabel; paymentState: ReturnPaymentLabel }
export interface OrderReturn { returnDate?: string; items: OrderReturnItem[] }
// fields added to Order:
//   shipmentState?: 'Shipped'|'Delivered'|'Ready'|'Pending'|'Delayed'|'Partial'|'Backorder'|'Canceled'
//   serviceStartDate?: string; cancellation?: CancellationRecord; etfByLine: Record<string, string>   // lineId -> label etf text
//   deliveries: OrderDelivery[]; returns: OrderReturn[]; createdAt: string; orderState: 'Open'|'Confirmed'|'Complete'|'Cancelled'
```
Mapping sources: `order.shipmentState`, `order.shippingInfo?.deliveries[]` → `OrderDelivery` (`items` = `delivery.items` joined to line names; `parcels[].trackingData.{trackingId, carrier}`; a parcel's own `items`), `order.returnInfo[]` → `OrderReturn` (`items[].lineItemId`, `shipmentState`, `paymentState`, `comment`), `order.custom.fields.serviceStartDate` / `cancellation` (JSON.parse in a try/catch → undefined on bad JSON) / `labelSnapshot` (JSON → `etfByLine` from each label's `etf`). **No tracking URL is built** (no carrier integration, D-059): the reference is shown as text.

### 4. Pure rules `lib/orders/postPurchaseRules.ts` (client-safe, no I/O) and config
`lib/config/postPurchase.ts`: `CANCEL_REASONS = ['changed_mind','better_offer','moving','service_not_needed','other'] as const`, `CANCEL_NOTE_MAX = 280`, `DEVICE_RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 30`, `RETURN_REASONS = ['defective','not_needed','wrong_item','other'] as const`, `RETURN_NOTE_MAX = 280`, `CANCEL_WINDOW_INCLUSIVE = false`. `lib/orders/now.ts`: `postPurchaseNow(): Date` = `new Date(Date.now() + days*86400000)` where `days = Number(process.env.DEV_NOW_OFFSET_DAYS)` **only when `NODE_ENV === 'development'`** and the value is a finite integer in [0, 400], else `new Date()` (so Chrome checks can age an order; never active in production).
```ts
export type CancelBlock = 'ALREADY_CANCELLED' | 'ORDER_COMPLETE' | 'SERVICE_STARTED' | 'NO_START_DATE' | 'EQUIPMENT_SHIPPED' | 'HAS_RETURN';
export function cancelEligibility(order: Pick<Order,'orderState'|'serviceStartDate'|'shipmentState'|'returns'>, now: Date): { allowed: true; until: string /* ISO date */ } | { allowed: false; block: CancelBlock };
// order of checks: Cancelled → ALREADY_CANCELLED; Complete → ORDER_COMPLETE; no start date → NO_START_DATE (fail closed);
// shipmentState in Shipped|Delivered|Partial → EQUIPMENT_SHIPPED; returns.length>0 → HAS_RETURN;
// now >= Date.parse(serviceStartDate + 'T00:00:00Z') (or > end of that day when CANCEL_WINDOW_INCLUSIVE) → SERVICE_STARTED; else allowed.
export type ReturnBlock = 'ORDER_CANCELLED' | 'WINDOW_CLOSED' | 'NO_RETURNABLE_LINES';
export interface ReturnableLine { lineItemId: string; name: string; quantityOrdered: number; quantityAlreadyRequested: number; quantityAvailable: number }
export function returnEligibility(order: Pick<Order,'orderState'|'createdAt'|'lines'|'returns'>, now: Date): { allowed: true; lines: ReturnableLine[]; until: string } | { allowed: false; block: ReturnBlock };
// window: now <= Date.parse(createdAt) + 30*86400000; returnable line = line.acquisition != null and quantityAvailable > 0 where quantityAvailable = quantity − Σ returned quantity for that lineItemId
export function buildCancelActions(order: OrderForCancel, input: { reason: CancelReason; note?: string }, now: Date): OrderUpdateAction[];
// [{action:'changeOrderState', orderState:'Cancelled'}, then the cancellation field]: if order.custom?.type key === 'malva-order' → {action:'setCustomField', name:'cancellation', value: JSON.stringify(record)}, else {action:'setCustomType', type:{typeId:'type', key:'malva-order'}, fields:{cancellation: JSON.stringify(record)}}
export function buildReturnActions(order: OrderForReturn, input: { items: {lineItemId:string; quantity:number}[]; reason: ReturnReason; note?: string }, now: Date): OrderUpdateAction[];
// [{action:'addReturnInfo', returnDate: now.toISOString(), items:[{ key:`ret-${yyyyMMddHHmmss}-${n}`, lineItemId, quantity, comment: `${reason}` + (note ? `: ${note}` : ''), shipmentState:'Advised' }]}, then the returnRequest field (same type rule as cancellation): value = JSON.stringify([...existingRequests, {requestedAt, reason, note?, lineItemIds}])]
export function validateCancelInput(body: unknown): { ok: true; value: {reason: CancelReason; note?: string} } | { ok: false; code: 'INVALID_REASON' | 'NOTE_REQUIRED' | 'NOTE_TOO_LONG' };   // reason 'other' requires a trimmed note 1..280; other reasons: note optional 0..280
export function validateReturnInput(body: unknown, lines: ReturnableLine[]): { ok: true; value: ... } | { ok: false; code: 'INVALID_ITEMS' | 'QUANTITY_TOO_HIGH' | 'INVALID_REASON' | 'NOTE_REQUIRED' | 'NOTE_TOO_LONG' };
```
`addReturnInfo` item fields (verified): `ReturnItemDraft { key?, quantity (required), lineItemId, comment?, shipmentState (required), custom? }`; the action takes `items` (required), `returnTrackingId?`, `returnDate?` ([OpenAPI `OrderAddReturnInfoAction`](https://docs.commercetools.com/api/projects/orders#add-returninfo)). Per the docs ReturnPaymentState starts `NonRefundable` for `Advised` items (platform-assigned; we do not set it).

### 5. Server module `lib/ct/post-purchase.ts` (`server-only`, `[SKILL: commercetools-storefront]`)
```ts
export async function getOwnedOrder(orderNumber: string, customerId: string): Promise<RawOrder | null>   // orders().withOrderNumber; null when missing or customerId differs
export async function cancelOrder(orderNumber: string, customerId: string, input: {reason; note?}): Promise<Order>
export async function requestReturn(orderNumber: string, customerId: string, input: ...): Promise<Order>
export class NotCancellableError extends Error { constructor(readonly block: CancelBlock) }
export class ReturnNotAllowedError extends Error { constructor(readonly code: 'ORDER_CANCELLED'|'WINDOW_CLOSED'|'NO_RETURNABLE_LINES'|'QUANTITY_TOO_HIGH') }
```
`cancelOrder` (idempotent; one 409 retry that **re-reads and re-checks eligibility**):
1. `getOwnedOrder` (null → `OrderNotFoundError`). If `orderState === 'Cancelled'` → return the mapped order unchanged (200 on a repeated click).
2. `cancelEligibility(order, postPurchaseNow())` not allowed → `NotCancellableError(block)`.
3. **Stop monthly charges first:** `GET /recurring-orders?where=originOrder(id="<orderId>")&limit=50`; for each whose `recurringOrderState` is not already `Canceled`: `POST /recurring-orders/{id}` `{ version, actions: [{ action: 'setRecurringOrderState', recurringOrderState: { type: 'canceled', reason: 'customer-cancelled-order' } }] }` (verified: `RecurringOrderSetStateAction.recurringOrderState` is the draft union `active|canceled|expired|paused`; `canceled` accepts an optional `reason` string; needs `manage_recurring_orders`, OA-02). If any call fails → throw (nothing else changed), the buyer sees a retryable error; calling cancel again continues because step 3 skips the ones already canceled.
4. `POST /orders/{id}` `{ version, actions: buildCancelActions(order, input, now) }`.
5. Re-map and return the order. Never log the note text.
`requestReturn`: `getOwnedOrder`; `returnEligibility` (not allowed → `ReturnNotAllowedError`); `validateReturnInput` against `lines`; **one** `POST /orders/{id}` with `buildReturnActions`; 409 → re-read, re-check remaining quantity (a double submit fails with `QUANTITY_TOO_HIGH`, so **no duplicate return** is created); return the mapped order.
`mapOrder` is S's mapper (V appended fields, §3).

### 6. Routes (`private, no-store`; `{ error: { code, message } }` shape from E; every route first requires `session.customerId` → else 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`)
| Route | Body | Success | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/orders/[orderNumber]/cancel` | `{ reason: CancelReason, note?: string }` | 200 `{ order: Order }` | 400 `INVALID_REASON`/`NOTE_REQUIRED`/`NOTE_TOO_LONG`; 404 `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`; 409 `NOT_CANCELLABLE { block }`; 502 `CANCEL_FAILED` (recurring or order write failed; safe to retry) |
| `POST /api/orders/[orderNumber]/return` | `{ items: { lineItemId: string; quantity: number }[], reason: ReturnReason, note?: string }` | 200 `{ order: Order }` | 400 `INVALID_ITEMS`/`QUANTITY_TOO_HIGH`/`INVALID_REASON`/`NOTE_REQUIRED`/`NOTE_TOO_LONG`; 404; 409 `ORDER_CANCELLED`/`WINDOW_CLOSED`/`NO_RETURNABLE_LINES` |
`orderNumber` must match U's `^MLV-[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{8}$` before any call (else 404). Hook `hooks/useOrderActions.ts`: `cancel(orderNumber, input)`, `requestReturn(orderNumber, input)` → both call the route, then `mutate(keyOrder(orderNumber), order, false)` and `mutate(KEY_ORDERS)` (S's keys) so the detail page and list update without reload.

### 7. UI (appended to S's order detail page `app/[locale]/account/orders/[orderNumber]/page.tsx`; components in `components/orders/`; tokens only; design not drawn: Junior design choice, D-068; documented here with a one-line rationale in the PR/commit message)
Page sections, **in this order after S's summary/lines**: `CancellationNotice` (only when cancelled) → `OrderActions` (cancel box + return box) → `ShipmentSection` → `ReturnsSection`.
- **`OrderActions` / cancel box** (card `--radius-xl`, border `--color-border`): when `cancelEligibility.allowed`: text "You can cancel this order until {date}." (date = `serviceStartDate − 1 day`, formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale,{dateStyle:'long',timeZone:'UTC'})`; for `CANCEL_WINDOW_INCLUSIVE` = the start date) and an outlined pill button **"Cancel order"**. When blocked: sentence per block (below) + link "Contact support" → `/support`. Dialog `CancelOrderDialog` (client): title `Cancel order {orderNumber}?`; intro "This cancels the whole order, including your monthly plans. This can't be undone."; radio group "Why are you cancelling?" (5 options, required); textarea "Tell us more" (visible for all; **required and labelled "(required)" for "Other"**; counter x/280); a bordered block "Early-termination fee": one row per service line `{name}: {etf}`, then the sentence from §1; buttons ghost **"Keep my order"** and danger-filled pill **"Cancel order"** (disabled until a reason is chosen and, for Other, a note typed; shows a spinner and is disabled while the request runs; `aria-busy`). On success the dialog closes, a `role="status"` toast "Order cancelled." appears and the page re-renders cancelled; on `NOT_CANCELLABLE` the dialog shows the block message and a "Close" button; on network error "We couldn't cancel your order. Try again." with the button re-enabled (safe: idempotent).
- Block messages (`orders.cancel.block.*`): `SERVICE_STARTED` "Your service has started, so this order can't be cancelled online."; `NO_START_DATE` "This order can't be cancelled online."; `EQUIPMENT_SHIPPED` "Your equipment has already shipped, so this order can't be cancelled online."; `HAS_RETURN` "This order has a return request, so it can't be cancelled online."; `ALREADY_CANCELLED`/`ORDER_COMPLETE` render no cancel box (state tag already says it).
- **`CancellationNotice`**: banner `--color-danger` on `pink-50`: "This order was cancelled on {date}." + "Reason: {label}" (+ the note in quotes) + "No further charges will be made."
- **Return box** (below cancel box, same card style, only when the order has at least one line with `acquisition`): allowed → text "You can return a device until {date} (30 days after ordering)." and button **"Return a device"**; blocked → `WINDOW_CLOSED` "The 30-day return window for this order has ended." / `ORDER_CANCELLED` hidden / `NO_RETURNABLE_LINES` "Every device on this order already has a return request." `ReturnRequestDialog`: table of returnable lines with a quantity stepper `0…quantityAvailable` (QuantityStepper from I; at least one > 0), reason select (`defective` "It's faulty", `not_needed` "I don't need it", `wrong_item` "Wrong item", `other` "Other" → note required), note textarea; sentence "We'll record your request on your order. Return instructions are not sent automatically in this version." Buttons "Cancel" / **"Request return"**. After success the dialog closes, toast "Return requested." and `ReturnsSection` shows the new item.
- **`ShipmentSection`** (scenarios "Shipment state visible", "Partial shipment"): H2 "Shipments". Header tag from `order.shipmentState`: Pending "Preparing", Ready "Ready to ship", Shipped "Shipped", Partial "Partly shipped", Delivered "Delivered", Delayed "Delayed", Backorder "Backordered", Canceled "Shipment canceled". No deliveries → text "Nothing has shipped yet." (physical items) or, when the order has no physical lines (no line with `acquisition` and no equipment), the section is hidden. Each delivery = card "Shipment {n} of {total}" with created date; inside each parcel a row **"Parcel {m} of {k}"** with `Carrier: {carrier}` and `Tracking reference: {trackingId}` (monospace, copyable text; a missing reference shows "Tracking reference not available yet"), then the items of **that parcel** ("{quantity} × {name}"); when a parcel has no `items`, its delivery's items are listed under the delivery instead. Several parcels or deliveries are visually separate cards (never one aggregate status line).
- **`ReturnsSection`** (scenario "Refund state visible"): H2 "Returns" (hidden when `returns` is empty). Per request: date, then per item a row `{quantity} × {name}` with **two separate labelled lines**: `Goods: {Return requested | Received | Received, back in stock | Received, not resellable}` (`Advised`, `Returned`, `BackInStock`, `Unusable`) and `Refund: {Not due yet | Refund pending | Refunded | Not refunded}` (`NonRefundable`, `Initial`, `Refunded`, `NotRefunded`). The two lines use different icons/labels and never merge into one status; unknown values render the raw enum in muted text.
- Confirmation page (U, built **before** V) shows "Need to change your mind? You can cancel until {date}." using its own check `Date.now() < serviceStartDate`; V does not edit the confirmation page.

### 9. Pitfalls
1. `changeOrderState` does not touch payments, inventory or recurring orders: **cancel the recurring orders first** (§5.3) or the customer is still billed monthly.
2. Order version conflicts: the cancel/return write uses the freshly read order version; after a 409 re-read **and re-run eligibility** (an order may have shipped meanwhile).
3. Custom field type: an order whose finalize step failed has no `malva-order` type; `setCustomField` would fail → `buildCancelActions` / `buildReturnActions` branch on the type key (tested both ways).
4. Dates: `serviceStartDate` is a calendar date compared as `00:00 UTC` (no time zones in v1); all displayed dates use `timeZone: 'UTC'` to avoid showing the day before.
5. Returns are per **line item id**; a recurring/installment device line keeps its id on the order, so a second request for the same line must subtract earlier requests (§4).
6. `returnInfo` has no `status` of its own; the "request" is only the item `shipmentState: Advised`. Do not invent a state in the UI.
7. Do not echo the cancel/return `note` into logs, error messages or `PROJECT-FINDINGS.md`.
8. `DEV_NOW_OFFSET_DAYS` must be inert unless `NODE_ENV === 'development'` (test asserts it is ignored when `production`).
9. The demo script mutates only orders whose number it is given and refuses any project key other than the allow-listed one (F's guard).

## Unit tests (scenario → test)
| Scenario (exact title from the spec) | Capability | Test (file → `it(...)` name) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shipment state visible | `post-purchase-order-management` | `components/orders/ShipmentSection.test.tsx` → "Shipment state visible: the shipment and its tracking reference are shown against its items" |
| Partial shipment | `post-purchase-order-management` | `components/orders/ShipmentSection.test.tsx` → "Partial shipment: each parcel and its items are distinguishable, not one aggregate status" |
| Return started | `post-purchase-order-management` | `lib/ct/post-purchase.return.test.ts` → "Return started: the return is recorded against those items with its own shipment and refund state" |
| Refund state visible | `post-purchase-order-management` | `components/orders/ReturnsSection.test.tsx` → "Refund state visible: refund is shown distinctly from whether the goods were received" |
D-040 behaviours without a spec scenario are covered by named tests: `lib/ct/post-purchase.cancel.test.ts` ("cancels recurring orders before changing the order state", "stores the reason in the cancellation field", "repeat cancel is a no-op"), `lib/orders/postPurchaseRules.test.ts` ("cancel is blocked from the service-start day", "phone-only order is not cancellable online", "return window is 30 days"), `components/orders/CancelOrderDialog.test.tsx` ("shows the early-termination fee text from the label snapshot").

## Chrome verification (run by Claude)
Setup: `cd site && npm run dev -- --port 3010` against the seeded project (OA-02); customer `qa-v1@example.com` / `Malva-Test-123!` registered at `/en-US/register`; orders created with U's `npx tsx scripts/demo/place-test-order.ts --email qa-v1@example.com --skus <cable-24-sku>,<router-sku>` (order **C**, cable: service starts today+5), `--skus <phone-sku>` (order **P**, phone only: start today), `--skus <phone-sku>,<device-sku>` for a device on installments (order **D**), each prints `MLV-XXXXXXXX`. Pages: `http://localhost:3010/en-US/account/orders/<number>`.
- C-V-1 (needs U-17): signed out, open order C's URL → redirected to `/en-US/login?redirect=…`; signed in as **another** customer (register `qa-v2@example.com`) → the page shows S's not-found state; `POST /api/orders/<C>/cancel` via `evaluate_script` as qa-v2 → 404 `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`; as anonymous → 401.
- C-V-2: as qa-v1 on order C: cancel box text "You can cancel this order until {today+4 days}." and an outlined "Cancel order" button; no cancellation notice; shipments section "Nothing has shipped yet."; console clean; screenshot at 1280 px.
- C-V-3: click "Cancel order" → dialog "Cancel order MLV-…?" with the 5 reasons, the note box, and an "Early-termination fee" block listing **Cable 500: $10 x months remaining** (text exactly as on the Broadband Facts label of that order) and the sentence about cancelling before service starts; the red "Cancel order" button is disabled; choose "Other" → button still disabled, note marked "(required)"; type a 281-character note → counter turns `--color-danger` and the button disabled; set a valid note → enabled.
- C-V-4: confirm → network: `POST /api/orders/<C>/cancel` 200 with `order.orderState = "Cancelled"`; toast "Order cancelled."; page now shows the notice "This order was cancelled on {today}.", "Reason: Other" with the note, "No further charges will be made.", and **no** cancel box; MCP `read_orders where orderNumber="<C>"` → `orderState: Cancelled`, `custom.fields.cancellation` JSON with `reason`, `note`, `cancelledAt`; MCP `read_recurring_orders` for that order → every recurring order `recurringOrderState: Canceled`; the confirmation page `/en-US/order-confirmation/<C>` shows tag "Cancelled" and no success banner. Reload → unchanged; `POST …/cancel` again via `evaluate_script` → 200 (idempotent), no extra writes (order `version` unchanged).
- C-V-5: order P (phone only): cancel box says "Your service has started, so this order can't be cancelled online." with a "Contact support" link to `/en-US/support`; `POST /api/orders/<P>/cancel` → 409 `NOT_CANCELLABLE` `block: "SERVICE_STARTED"`; order unchanged (MCP).
- C-V-6: new cable order C2; restart the dev server with `DEV_NOW_OFFSET_DAYS=6` → C2 shows "can't be cancelled online" (start was today+5); restart with `DEV_NOW_OFFSET_DAYS=4` → still cancellable (until date unchanged); restart without the variable.
- C-V-7: `npx tsx scripts/demo/advance-order.ts --order <C2> --ship-two-parcels` then reload C2 → cancel box now "Your equipment has already shipped, so this order can't be cancelled online."; shipments section: tag "Partly shipped", **two** shipment cards ("Shipment 1 of 2", "Shipment 2 of 2"), parcels "Parcel 1 of …" with `Carrier: DemoPost` and `Tracking reference: DP000111/DP000222/DP000333`, each parcel's items listed under that parcel (Partial shipment); then `--ship-all` → tag "Shipped"; `--deliver` → tag "Delivered", tracking references still shown against the items (Shipment state visible).
- C-V-8: order D (device on installments): return box "You can return a device until {today+30 days} (30 days after ordering)." and button "Return a device"; click → dialog with one row (device name, stepper 0–1), reason select, note; "Request return" disabled until quantity ≥ 1; choose quantity 1, reason "It's faulty", submit → network `POST /api/orders/<D>/return` 200; toast "Return requested."; Returns section shows the device with `Goods: Return requested` and `Refund: Not due yet`; MCP `read_orders`: `returnInfo[0].items[0]` has `lineItemId`, `quantity:1`, `shipmentState:"Advised"`, `paymentState:"NonRefundable"`, `comment` starting `defective`; `custom.fields.returnRequest` is a JSON array with one entry.
- C-V-9 (needs C-V-8): the return box now says "Every device on this order already has a return request."; `POST …/return` again via `evaluate_script` → 400 `QUANTITY_TOO_HIGH`; MCP shows still exactly one return item; the cancel box on order D is blocked with "This order has a return request, so it can't be cancelled online."
- C-V-10 (needs C-V-8): `npx tsx scripts/demo/advance-order.ts --order <D> --seed-received-return --line <deviceLineItemId>` (a second return item in `Returned`): reload → that item shows `Goods: Received` and `Refund: Refund pending`; then `--refund` → `Refund: Refunded` while `Goods` still reads `Received` (Refund state visible: two separate lines, never one merged status); screenshot.
- C-V-11: `DEV_NOW_OFFSET_DAYS=31` → order D2 (fresh device order) shows "The 30-day return window for this order has ended."; `POST …/return` → 409 `WINDOW_CLOSED`; restart without the variable.
- C-V-12: order with no device (order C) → no return box at all; `POST …/return` with a router line id → 409/400 (not a device line), no write.
- C-V-13 (375 px): order C (cancel box + dialog), order D (return dialog, shipments, returns) at 375×812 → dialogs fit the viewport with internal scroll, buttons full width and reachable, no horizontal page scroll, focus returns to the opening button after closing; Escape closes dialogs.

## Manual tests (owner only)
None.

## Excluded
- Carrier integration, tracking links and delivery events from a real carrier: **D-059** (tracking is read from the Order's `trackingData` only; the demo script writes it).
- Return **processing** — return labels, receiving goods, restock/unusable decisions, refund money movement, Order Edit settlement for a refund (spec constraint "post-purchase change that affects the total is an Order Edit"): **D-040** ("processing out of scope"); the storefront reflects the platform's states and never sets them.
- Plan changes, upgrades, mid-term amendments, partial cancellation of single lines, cancellation after service start: **D-040** ("No plan changes").
- Reversal/refund of the payment on cancel: **D-040**/**D-059** (no billing system); copy promises no refund.
- Guest self-service cancel/return: **D-035** gives guests checkout only; they use `/support` (**D-034**).

- [ ] All tasks ticked, `npm run verify` passes.

- [ ] C- lines present; STATUS set to `Ready for review`; screenshots taken by Claude (C- checks); owner may comment (D-068).
- [ ] Cancel stops recurring orders before changing the order state (test and C-V-4 evidence); the cancellation reason is stored in `custom.fields.cancellation`.
- [ ] `DEV_NOW_OFFSET_DAYS` is inert in production (test); no note text is logged.
